title: Crossover watch: scratch diary and quick-runbook
content:
Context and purpose:
- Personal scratchpad for the crossover shift (02:00->10:00). Keep terse. Hand this to the next person at handoff or paste into main runbook if anything sticks.

Summary at takeover:
- Took over from Liam at 02:00. No active SEV, two noisy alerts in past 6h (connection flaps and transient OOMs on gpu-pool-3).
- Main open items: INF-2345 (db conn flapping), transient OOM cascade on endpoints/predict-vertical (tracked in PR #842 experiment), noisy 429s from dedicated-gateway under burst.

What I did quickly (mitigations applied):
1) INF-2345 (db connections):
   - Rolled a k8s patch to prod-gw (deployment/prod-gateway) to increase DB pool size from 100->200 (configmap + restart). Command: kubectl -n prod apply -f /tmp/prod-gw-pool-bump.yaml && kubectl rollout status deploy/prod-gateway -n prod
   - Observed dropped conns drop ~70% within 15m. Watching.
2) OOMs on gpu-pool-3:
   - Temporarily drained one node (node/gpu-3b) to avoid cascade: kubectl cordon node/gpu-3b && drain with evict (evict tolerant pods).
   - Noticed nginx-ingress backlog spikes on node 3; rebalanced by scale-up: autoscaler allowed a +1 node burst.
3) 429s from dedicated-gateway:
   - Applied a phase-1 rate-limit increase for customer tier 'pilot' in the gateway-rules; created a short-lived rule to allow current backlog to drain.

Immediate watch signals (what to look at in the next 2 hours):
- infra/metrics: db.connections. query: sum(pg_stat_activity_count) by (host) — look for >180 per host.
- gpu nodes: node_memory_MiB_* and gpu_utilization; check for processes hitting cgroups OOM.
- ingress: 5xx and 429 spikes; dashboard: prod->network->ingress-latency (last 24h).
- logs: search for "kvcache::miss" flood, indicates model cache misrouting.

Quick commands cheat-sheet (pasteable):
- tail logs for prod-gw: kubectl -n prod logs -f deploy/prod-gateway --since=10m
- roll back prod-gw patch: kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/prod-gateway --to-revision=3
- cordon + drain: kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- check DB connections on primary: psql -h db-prod-1 -c "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;"

Open follow-ups (assign or note):
- PR #842 (runtime): experiment with smaller kv-cache retention on predict-vertical. If enabled, may reduce OOMs. Needs load test and observability hooks. Assigned: Priya.
- INF-2345: Add sensible backpressure on the gateway for short TTL spikes (instead of raising pool size permanently). Proposal doc TODO. Assigned: Maya (me) to draft.
- Add an alert to avoid silently scaling DB pool without owner: alert name "DBPoolAutoBump" that triggers on >2 config changes in 24h.

User-facing customer notes (if asked):
- If customer asks about increased latency: "We saw transient connection errors and applied mitigations to reduce dropped requests. We're monitoring and will post a timeline if impact grows."

Escalation/contact matrix:
- SRE lead: Priya Nair (pager)
- Runtime oncall: Liam O'Connor (slack/pager)
- Eng manager for prod: Rachel Kim (email)

Questions for next shift / unknowns:
- Why did autoscaler pick that particular node? Check cluster-autoscaler logs (possible bin-packing issue).
- Was there a concurrent deployment around 01:45? Check CI deploy history for prod-gateway (CI job id ~ 2026-03-10T01:40).

Notes to the next oncall (quick handoff bullets):
- Check INF-2345: if DB connections go >220 on any host, rollback pool bump and escalate to DB infra.
- Keep an eye on gpu-pool-3: if OOMs resume despite node drain, re-enable grpc-request-limits on predict-vertical to protect model servers (config flag: PRED_LIMIT_REQS).
- If 5xx rate >1% for more than 10m, flip the routing fallback to model-variant "low-memory-quant" for heavy endpoints (route policy id: rp-lowmem-03).

Low priority TODOs (can wait for next day):
- Add runbook section for incremental DB pool bumps: threshold, owner, rollback plan.
- Run a canary loadtest for PR #842 on staging with 75% production QPS.
- Review autoscaler config for gpu clusters to avoid draining during rolling updates.

Random scribbles / reminders to self:
- 03/11: ping infra about node labelling for gpu-3* (labels inconsistent).
- Save profiler traces from 02:22 (predict-vertical) -> logs path /tmp/trace-20260310-0222.prof

Handoff checklist (what I will tell next person verbally):
- We bumped DB pool; things improved, but watch for slow queries and slow clients that may saturate new capacity.
- One drained GPU node; watch weight of remaining pods.
- Alerts suppressed for 20m to avoid noisy duplicates; will unsuppress at 04:00 unless patterns remain.

End of notes. If you take over, add your initials + time at top and scribble any immediate actions you performed.

-- Maya C. (02:55)
